question: What is the primary purpose of isolation in a healthcare setting?

options.A: To interrupt the transmission of pathogenic microorganisms
options.B: To completely eliminate all bacteria from the hospital ward
options.C: To punish patients who fail to comply with hygiene rules
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of treating chronic illnesses

explanation: Separating infected patients physically restricts the spread of pathogens to susceptible individuals within the facility. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h1)

question: Why are immunocompromised patients particularly targeted for protection through isolation protocols?

options.A: They always harbor airborne multidrug-resistant organisms
options.B: Their natural defense mechanisms are weakened, making them prone to severe infections
options.C: Their metabolic rate prevents standard medications from working effectively
options.D: They require higher doses of intravenous antibiotics than other patients

explanation: Patients with depressed immunity cannot easily fight off opportunistic microbes picked up from the hospital environment. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h1)

question: Which link in the chain of infection is primarily targeted when implementing barrier isolation precautions?
explanation: Barriers like gloves, gowns, and masks directly block the pathway pathogens use to travel from the source to a new host. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h2)

question: A patient coughs and expels droplets containing Mycobacterium tuberculosis into the air. What link in the chain of infection does the cough represent?
explanation: The respiratory tract acts as the route through which the pathogen leaves the infected individual's body. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h2)

question: To which group of patients do standard precautions apply?

options.A: Individuals showing active symptoms of respiratory illness
options.B: All patients regardless of their diagnosis or infection status
options.C: Only patients confirmed to have a bloodborne pathogen
options.D: Patients admitted exclusively to intensive care units

explanation: Standard precautions form the baseline level of infection control for every single patient interaction in healthcare. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h3)

question: What is the primary rationale for applying standard precautions universally rather than selectively?

options.A: Laboratory test results are always available immediately upon admission
options.B: Many infected individuals may be asymptomatic or undiagnosed
options.C: Hospital accreditation agencies require universal charting for all supplies
options.D: It eliminates the need for handwashing between different patients

explanation: Because infectious status is not always known, treating all bodily fluids with caution prevents accidental exposure. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h3)

question: Which type of room ventilation is required for a patient placed on airborne precautions?
explanation: Negative pressure keeps air from flowing out into the hallway when the door is opened, trapping airborne droplet nuclei inside. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h4)

question: A patient is admitted with a confirmed diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis. Which specific barrier protection must the nurse wear when entering this room?
explanation: Tuberculosis spreads via airborne droplet nuclei, necessitating a fitted respirator that filters out tiny suspended particles. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h4)

question: According to standard protocol, which item of personal protective equipment is typically removed first during doffing?
explanation: Gloves are considered the most contaminated item and are removed first to prevent transferring pathogens to other parts of the body or clothing. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h5)

question: Why is performing hand hygiene immediately after removing personal protective equipment critical?

options.A: Microorganisms may have transferred to the hands during the removal process
options.B: Soap activates the residual chemicals left behind on discarded gowns
options.C: It cools down the skin after wearing non-breathable plastic gloves
options.D: Hospital policy mandates tracking hand hygiene frequency per shift

explanation: Even with careful technique, accidental contact with outer surfaces of PPE can contaminate the hands during doffing. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h5)

question: What should be done with diagnostic equipment like stethoscopes used on a patient in strict isolation?

options.A: Share them freely across all beds in the general ward
options.B: Wipe them with water and return them to the central station
options.C: Keep them dedicated inside the patient's room
options.D: Submerge them in boiling water after every single use

explanation: Using dedicated equipment prevents the inadvertent mechanical transfer of pathogens to non-isolated patients. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h6)

question: Why must soiled linen from an isolation room be handled with minimal agitation?

options.A: To prevent aerosolizing infectious pathogens into the surrounding air
options.B: To ensure the fabric color does not fade during chemical processing
options.C: To reduce the electrical power consumed by hospital laundry services
options.D: To keep the laundry from tearing before reaching the washing machine

explanation: Shaking or tossing contaminated linen disperses dust and microbes into the atmosphere, creating an inhalation hazard. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h6)

question: Which psychological response is most commonly observed in patients placed under prolonged isolation?

options.A: Complete memory loss of the admission event

explanation: Sensory deprivation and separation from social support networks frequently trigger depressive symptoms in isolated patients. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h7)

question: What is NOT a recommended nursing strategy for mitigating the psychosocial impact of isolation?

options.A: Scheduling regular check-ins to address patient fears and concerns
options.B: Limiting all verbal communication to prevent staff contamination
options.C: Explaining the clinical reasons behind the isolation precautions clearly
options.D: Facilitating video calls between the patient and their family members

explanation: Cutting off verbal interaction increases feelings of abandonment; nurses should communicate regularly while wearing appropriate barriers. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h7)

question: Whose primary responsibility is it to monitor and enforce visitor compliance with isolation guidelines on a hospital ward?
explanation: Nurses coordinate direct patient care environments and actively educate and monitor visitors regarding proper PPE usage. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h8)

question: Why is accurate charting of isolation protocols by the nurse critical for the wider healthcare facility?

options.A: It replaces the need for verbal shift handovers at the nursing station
options.B: It proves to patients that their room charges are fully justified
options.C: It ensures continuity of care and alerts all multidisciplinary team members to safety requirements
options.D: It calculates the exact financial bonus due to the nursing staff each month

explanation: Clear documentation informs every incoming clinician and support worker about necessary barrier precautions before room entry. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h8)
